title: Minimum Sum After Removing K From Ends
statement:
You are given an array `a` of `n` integers (values may be negative) and an integer `k`. You must delete **exactly** `k` elements from the array, one at a time. Each deletion may only remove the **first** or the **last** element of the array as it currently stands, so you can never delete an element from the middle while elements are still on either side of it.

After the `k` deletions, add up the elements that remain. Return the **minimum** possible value of that sum. If every element is deleted (`k = n`), the remaining sum is `0`.
inputFormat:
The first line contains two integers `n` and `k`.
The second line contains `n` integers `a[0] ... a[n-1]`.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the minimum possible sum of the remaining elements.

examples.explanation: Delete one element from the front (6) and one from the back (9). The remaining elements are 1, -4, -3 with sum -6, which is the smallest of all choices (delete two from the front: -4 + -3 + 9 = 2; delete two from the back: 6 + 1 + -4 = 3).
All elements are deleted, so nothing remains and the sum is 0.
No deletions are made, so the sum of the whole array is returned.

hints: If you delete i elements from the front, you must delete k - i from the back. What does the remaining part of the array look like?
Whatever split you choose, the remaining elements form one contiguous block of exactly n - k elements.
So the answer is the minimum sum over all windows of length n - k. Slide the window and update its sum in O(1) per step.
